marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q015.takeaway: The appendix of the epididymis is a mesonephric (Wolffian) duct remnant; the appendix of the testis is Müllerian.
marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q015.displayText:
Appendix of the epididymis is a derivative of the mesonephric duct.

Appendix of the testis is a derivative of the paramesonephric duct.

rationales.a: The appendix of the testis is a remnant of the paramesonephric (Müllerian) duct, not the mesonephric duct.
rationales.c: The prostatic utricle is a Müllerian remnant in the male and is not derived from the mesonephric duct.
rationales.d: The Fallopian tube develops from the unfused cranial part of the paramesonephric duct, not the mesonephric duct.

marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q016.takeaway: A unicornuate uterus results from failure of development of one Müllerian (paramesonephric) duct.
marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q016.displayText:
A unicornuate uterus is a Mullerian anomaly caused due to the defect in the formation or fusion of paired Mullerian ducts.

The uterus and the cervix develop from the paramesonephric ducts (Mullerian ducts).

rationales.b: Wolffian duct is another name for the mesonephric duct and primarily contributes to the male genital duct system, not formation of the uterus.
rationales.c: The mesonephric duct does not form the uterus; the uterine body and cervix are Müllerian derivatives.
rationales.d: The urogenital sinus contributes to lower urinary and genital structures, including the lower vaginal developmental pathway, but it does not form the uterus.

marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q017.takeaway: The organ of Rosenmüller (epoophoron) is a female remnant of mesonephric tubules.
marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q017.displayText:
The organ of Rosenmuller, also known as epoophoron, is a remnant of the mesonephric tubule in females.

The mesonephros consists of a series of excretory tubules that develop in the thoracolumbar region. The mesonephric tubules drain into the mesonephric duct. Most of the mesonephric tubules disappear, but some mesonephric tubules take part in the formation of the efferent ductules in males.

The mesonephric tubules give rise to the following structures and remnants:
• Females: epoophoron and paroophoron
• Males: efferent ductules (ductuli efferentes or vasa efferentia), lobules of the head of the epididymis, and paradidymis.

rationales.a: The endodermal urogenital sinus does not give rise to the epoophoron; the epoophoron is a mesonephric-tubule remnant.
rationales.b: The Müllerian duct is the paramesonephric duct and forms major female reproductive-tract structures, but the epoophoron comes from mesonephric tubules.
rationales.d: Paramesonephric duct is synonymous with Müllerian duct; neither is the source of the organ of Rosenmüller.

marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q018.takeaway: The vagina has dual embryologic origin: upper vagina from Müllerian ducts and lower vagina from the urogenital sinus.
marrow__ANAT_CH10_Q018.displayText:
The vagina has a dual origin: the upper portion is derived from the Mullerian duct (paramesonephric duct) and the lower portion is derived from the cloaca (urogenital sinus).

The solid tips of the paramesonephric ducts come in contact with the urogenital sinus. Two solid evaginations, called the sinovaginal bulbs, develop from the pelvic part of the urogenital sinus. The sinovaginal bulbs proliferate to become a solid vaginal plate. This entire plate is canalized by the 5th month to form the vagina.

The upper part of the vagina is derived from the Mullerian duct, while the lower part is derived from the urogenital sinus. The vaginal fornices are of paramesonephric origin.

rationales.a: Ectoderm alone does not account for the vagina’s dual embryologic origin.
rationales.b: Mesoderm alone is incomplete because the lower vaginal developmental contribution comes through the endodermal urogenital sinus.
rationales.c: The tested dual origin is not ectoderm plus mesoderm; it is Müllerian duct plus the urogenital-sinus contribution from the cloacal region.
